title: Joiner edits relationship details and gets an unexplained failure
preconditions: A created the space; B joined as the partner.
B opens Account and chooses Edit relationship.
B changes the anniversary date and saves.

actions.note: B opens Edit relationship and saves a new date.

expected_behavior: A non-creator is either not offered the edit action or told plainly that only the creator can change space details.
A failed save explains the rule and preserves the current values.
The UI never implies that the partner's change was saved.
candidate_failure_modes: The partner taps a working-looking Edit relationship row, fills the form, and receives only "Unable to save. Please try again."
The partner retries because the message implies a transient network problem.
The partner believes the anniversary date changed when the server rejected it.

observed_code_behavior: Spaces enforce one active membership per user and one active partner per space at the storage layer.
Joining redeems an invite once; an expired or already-redeemed code is rejected, and a historical partner slot is permanently bound.
Leaving flips the caller's membership to left and keeps shared history for the remaining member.
Space hydration, foreground refresh, and mutation callbacks are scoped to the signed-in user id.
documented_requirement: A non-creator is either not offered the edit action or told plainly that only the creator can change space details.
A failed save explains the rule and preserves the current values.
The UI never implies that the partner's change was saved.
hypothetical_user_behavior:
A fictional participant (Alice Moreau) said: "Okay, going through this as someone who just wants to save little moments with my partner and not think about it again:

Three things I would remove without blinking:
1. The storage meter. I have never once looked at it. If it filled up I would find out when something failed to save, which is the only moment I'd actually care. It exists to make me anxious, that's the whole job.
2. The upgrade prompts / feature gates. I hit "save" and get told about a tier. That's the exact "this became a chore" feeling I was trying to avoid. If the free version can't hold a photo of a Tuesday, just say so once, at signup, and never again.
3. The plan explanation page. I don't read secondary explanations. I pressed the primary button. The page exists so someone can say they explained it, not so I can understand it.

The one thing I'd keep: the preview that shows up after I save. That little thumbnail is the only proof I trust that the note actually exists and my partner can see it. Take that away and I'd save everything twice out of doubt — which costs you more storage than the meter ever saved anyone.

Worth saying out loud: "why does this even exist" is a great question for the copy too. Half the lines around the paywall are apologizing for the paywall instead of removing it."
Alice Moreau assumes: an invitation shared means the partner has joined
Alice Moreau assumes: deleting a memory removes it for both people
Bob Whitfield assumes: creating an account is the same as joining Alice's space
